card.name: The word one before a counted thing
card.fires_on: The word "one" (sometimes "two", "multiple" or a digit) used as a count right before a unit noun such as dose, capsule, vial, case or platform.

modes.label: One before a dose item
modes.description: "one" quantifies a single dose, capsule or vial.
modes.example: Do not take more than<< one>> dose in 24 hours.

modes.label: One starting a case report
modes.description: Capitalized "One" opens a sentence describing a single patient or case.
modes.example: 6,400 mg (single dose):<< One>> case in the literature reported one patient who

modes.label: Other small counts
modes.description: "two", "multiple" or a digit in a range stands before a counted noun.
modes.example: Heart failure has been observed with<< two>> other members of the DPP-4

card.writes: It favors count-like nouns for small countable things, such as grains, pixels, molecules, cells and calories, and suppresses piece-type words.
card.plain: It marks a small number like "one" that is about to be followed by the thing being counted.
